# Topic Modeling Chinese Media Newspapers

### Process into corpus object

```{r}
textdata <- China %>% 
  select(filename, sentence, published_date) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rename(doc_id = filename, text= sentence) %>%
  mutate(
    parsed_date = ymd(published_date),
    year = lubridate::year(parsed_date)
  ) %>%
  mutate(year=year(published_date))

```

### Remove stopwords, clean corpus

```{r}
# 1. Define standard stopwords
english_stopwords <- stopwords("en")

# 2. Build corpus
corpus <- Corpus(DataframeSource(textdata))

# 3. Clean in correct sequence
processedCorpus <- tm_map(corpus, content_transformer(tolower))
processedCorpus <- tm_map(processedCorpus, removePunctuation, preserve_intra_word_dashes = TRUE)
processedCorpus <- tm_map(processedCorpus, removeNumbers)

# Remove stopwords BEFORE stemming
processedCorpus <- tm_map(processedCorpus, removeWords, english_stopwords)

# Stem documents after removing stopwords
processedCorpus <- tm_map(processedCorpus, stemDocument, language = "en")
processedCorpus <- tm_map(processedCorpus, stripWhitespace)
```

```{r tm3a}
#DTM: rows correspond to the documents in the corpus. Columns correspond to the terms in the documents. Cells correspond to the weights of the terms. (Girder)
# compute document term matrix with terms >= minimumFrequency
minimumFrequency <- 5
DTM <- DocumentTermMatrix(processedCorpus, control = list(bounds = list(global = c(minimumFrequency, Inf))))
# have a look at the number of documents and terms in the matrix
dim(DTM)
# due to vocabulary pruning, we have empty rows in our DTM
# LDA does not like this. So we remove those docs from the
# DTM and the metadata
sel_idx <- slam::row_sums(DTM) > 0
DTM <- DTM[sel_idx, ]
textdata <- textdata[sel_idx, ]
#5 term minimum[1] 1387 3019
#5 term minimum[1] 308597 10339

```

```{r tm12}
# number of topics
# K <- 20
K <- 6
# set random number generator seed
set.seed(9161)
#Latent Dirichlet Allocation, LDA
topicModel2 <- LDA(DTM, K, method="Gibbs", control=list(iter = 500, verbose = 25, alpha = 0.2))
tmResult <- posterior(topicModel2)
theta <- tmResult$topics
beta <- tmResult$terms
topicNames <- apply(terms(topicModel2, 10), 2, paste, collapse = " ")  # reset topicnames
```

### Mean topic proportions per year

```{r}
# Step 1: Check dimensions
n_theta <- nrow(theta)
n_textdata <- length(textdata$year)

cat("Number of rows in theta: ", n_theta, "\n")
cat("Number of documents in textdata: ", n_textdata, "\n")

# Check if textdata contains all the documents in theta
common_ids <- intersect(rownames(theta), textdata$doc_id) # Assuming textdata has a 'doc_id' column

# Filter textdata to include only the documents present in theta
textdata_filtered <- textdata[textdata$doc_id %in% common_ids, ]

# Check dimensions after filtering
n_textdata_filtered <- nrow(textdata_filtered)
cat("Number of documents in filtered textdata: ", n_textdata_filtered, "\n")

# Ensure the lengths match now
if (n_theta != n_textdata_filtered) {
  stop("The number of rows in 'theta' still does not match the length of 'textdata_filtered$decade'.")
}

# Align rownames of theta with filtered textdata
theta_aligned <- theta[rownames(theta) %in% textdata_filtered$doc_id, ]

# Optional: Verify the order of documents
if (!all(rownames(theta_aligned) == textdata_filtered$doc_id)) {
  # If the order doesn't match, reorder one to match the other
  textdata_filtered <- textdata_filtered[match(rownames(theta_aligned), textdata_filtered$doc_id), ]
}

# Ensure they are now aligned and can be combined
if (!all(rownames(theta_aligned) == textdata_filtered$doc_id)) {
  stop("The document IDs still do not match. Please check the data alignment.")
}

# Step 2: Combine data
topic_data <- data.frame(theta_aligned, year = textdata_filtered$year)

# Step 3: Aggregate data
topic_proportion_per_year <- aggregate(. ~ year, data = topic_data, FUN = mean)


# get mean topic proportions per decade
# topic_proportion_per_decade <- aggregate(theta, by = list(decade = textdata$decade), mean)
# set topic names to aggregated columns
colnames(topic_proportion_per_year)[2:(K+1)] <- topicNames
# reshape data frame
vizDataFrame <- melt(topic_proportion_per_year, id.vars = "year")

# #filter out 1960 - one article
vizDataFrame <- vizDataFrame %>% 
   filter(!year==2026)
```

#Memo 250 words

Topic modeling with the dataframe of Chinese papers covering Xinjiang women has produced six topics that were surprisingly relevant to the content of those 205 articles. The most relevant were topics #1 - narratives ("said peopl time year women one also uyghur mani told"), #2 - rights reports ("china right human state countri intern report hong forc kong"), #3 - reeducation ("educ train religi news law ethnic govern extrem group center") and #5 - china minorities ("china xinjiang develop peopl region percent tibet year countri ethnic"). The first three topics were most relevant. The word "mani" in topic #1 was puzzling to me, so I started reading articles in textdata file with keyword search. Most articles refer to political or economic "manipulation" by the US or the West in general, the word "manipulated" also appeared often, together with "manifesto" and "manifestation" (i.e. "manifesto of theocracy" as described in one article). Overall, it was more or less clear that topic #1 was a general description of who said what, who told what, about women and about Uyghurs. For topic #2, the articles suggest the reports by international human rights organizations that are "hostile" or "critical" of China. The word "forc" refers to "forced", which can relate to either forced labor of Uyghurs, or forced abortions and sterilizations of women. The topic #3 has a distinct them about the reasons why such things happen in China's Xinjiang, for example, people there undergo "educ"(education), "train"(training), there are certain "law"s that govern "ethnic" minorities and their "religi"on and some "extrem"ist groups. The topic #5 broadly is about ethnic minorities not only in Xinjiang, but also Tibet. There are articles that describe government policies to develop these regions, bring jobs, prosperity and education to those communities. The topics #4 ("time end global document reserv copyright right provid classif language english") and #6 ("china xinjiang region uyghur autonom associ northwest photo word length") are not so relevant as the former mainly has articles that describe the origin of the word "genocide" in English language, while the latter mainly refers to the location of the region. 
One issue I had with ggplot is that it does not show all 6 topics, only 5 and NA. I tried to fix it with AI but it got worse, increasing NA space. I am not sure where to problem is, after all.
